title: Short Stuff: Atacama Skeleton
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Atacama skeleton, a small mummified humanoid remains found in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile, in the abandoned nitrate mining town of Llanos de Lenoria (transcribed as Ladnoria/Lenoria). The hosts cover its alien-theorist appeal, the Atacama Desert's preservation conditions, how treasure hunter Oscar Munoz allegedly obtained it, its sale to Ramon Navia Osorio, ufologist Steven Greer's involvement with the documentary Sirius, the 2018 Genome Research DNA study by a team led by Gary Nolan showing human DNA with multiple genetic mutations, likely a stillborn or prematurely born baby girl, and the ethical and legal backlash in Chile over unauthorized excavation and the remains not being repatriated.

entities.name: Institute for Research and Exo Biological Studies

segments.title: Introduction and alien speculation
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Atacama skeleton, a small skeleton with a conical skull and ten pairs of ribs, and note UFO enthusiasts' claims that it was an alien.

segments.title: Atacama Desert and Lenoria
segments.summary: The skeleton is partly mummified. The hosts describe the Atacama Desert's dryness and the abandoned nitrate mining town of Lenoria, and note the Chinchorro culture's mummification tradition.

segments.title: Oscar Munoz and the sale to Navia Osorio
segments.summary: Treasure hunter Oscar Munoz claimed he found the skeleton on a shelf in Lenoria, though most say it came from a burial site. It was later sold to Ramon Navia Osorio, a Spanish collector and president of a UFO enthusiast organization.

segments.title: Cliffhanger break
segments.summary: Hosts tease the next part of the story before a break.

segments.title: Steven Greer and the Sirius documentary
segments.summary: Ufologist Steven Greer proposed extracting DNA for the documentary Sirius. Microbiologist Gary Nolan offered to run a genomic test.

segments.title: DNA results: human baby girl
segments.summary: The DNA was found to be modern, abundant, high quality and human. The 2018 Genome Research paper indicated a likely stillborn or prematurely born baby girl with multiple genetic mutations.

segments.title: Age and possible family
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the remains likely being under five hundred years old, though possibly only decades old, meaning parents could still be alive, and note the age puzzle given the town's abandonment.

segments.title: Ethical and legal backlash
segments.summary: Chilean scientific groups condemned the study as unethical and illegal since it lacked authorization from the Council of National Monuments. The researchers acknowledged the ethical lapse, and said the remains should be repatriated.

segments.title: Remains still in Spain
segments.summary: The body remains with Ramon Navia Osorio in Spain and has not been returned to Chile. Steven Greer disputes the human findings.
